LESSON: MASS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: Measurement
Topic 2.2: Mass
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Mass, part of Measurement in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can you compare the mass of two or more objects?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Collect safe objects of different mass from their immediate environment. Learners with manipulative difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, assistive technology, be assisted by peers, learner support assistants or the teacher to collect objects. Safety of all learners should be observed

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Collect safe objects of different mass from their immediate environment. Learners with manipulative difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, assistive technology, be assisted by peers, learner support assistants or the teacher to collect objects. Safety of all learners should be observed

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Mass together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: learner discusses objects that are heavier, lighter or have the same mass.

● Digital literacy: learner uses digital devices to play games involving mass.

18

Values:
● Unity: learner appreciates the effort of others as they measure mass of different items.

● Respect: learner gives others equal opportunity as they use safe objects to identify heavier, lighter or objects of the

same mass.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Safety issues: learner observes safety as they collect objects of different mass from their immediate environment.

● Effective communication: learner listens and contributes in discussion on objects that are heavier, lighter or have the

same mass.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner is able to relate the concept of safe objects from the environment to the concept of safety in the school environment

in Environmental Activities.
